messages.author: 6db62e08ec862130
messages.subject: autodiff of model with some parameters fixed, optimization
parts:
hessian() in stan/agrad/autodiff.hpp treats all model values as if they
are free. For example, if you have a 2 dimensional multivariate normal
density then there are 5 potential parameters, 2 means and the lower
triangle of the covariance matrix (2 variance and 1 covariance).
However, suppose one of the variances is fixed to 1. Ideally, the
Hessian should omit any pairs involving the fixed variance.

Is there any C++ API facility to omit fixed parameters? Is something
planned?

--

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] autodiff of model with some parameters fixed, optimization
parts:
Stan has no mechanism to "fix" a defined parameter.  You should instead define the model so that those parameters are not included.  See section 7.2 in the manual for details.

Cheers,
Marcus

I have another question about the autodiff stuff.

hessian() appears to evaluate the log_prob() at least once for each
parameter. If I dig into multi_normal_log, I see that this function
calls trace_inv_quad_form_ldlt which solves ldlt_Sigma (takes the matrix
inverse). This seems a bit inefficient given that matrix inverse can be
fairly expensive. Is there some way to optimize this using a cache or
memoized result? Or do I misunderstand the performance bottleneck here?

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] autodiff, optimization
parts:
There is no easy way to optimize this and it's not clear that it's worth it.  Either Sigma is a parameter (in which case, it needs to be refactorized each time) or it's data (in which case the factorization is likely not a major cost unless the dimensionality is huge).

Also, note that right now hessian() uses a finite diff approximation to the Hessian.  In the (hopefully near) future it will use autodiff and avoid this issue altogether.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] autodiff, optimization
parts:
You're looking at two different things.

Joshua is talking about the hessian() function in autodiff.hpp,
and it is indeed as he describes it.

Marcus is talking about our use of the Hessian to calculate
Laplace approximations to covariance at a mode.

To answer Joshua's original question, each time the density is evaluated,
it's with a different forward-mode variable configuration. As far as we
can tell, it's not possible to reuse a factorization with our current
reverse-nested-in-forward autodiff setup for Hessians.

We're working on a new approach to autodiff which is much faster
for Hessians (an order of magnitude or more) for just this reason.

- Bob
